name: Concealed Quadrille
summary: Four-player trick-taking game over 8 hands of 5 tricks. Players bid for the contract, the Taker names trumps and secretly calls a partner (or plays solo), and the hand is scored to zero sum.

player.meaning: tricks won over the whole game, used as the tie-break
tricks won in the current hand, reset each hand
card codes held, shown by name and code
this hand's bid (0 = Pass, else 3, 4 or 5)
privately told: you are the Taker's partner in this hand (call only)
code of the card played to the current trick
card power of played_card in the current trick

game.meaning: trump suit number t (1 Spades, 2 Clubs, 3 Hearts, 4 Diamonds)
seat named by the Taker; equal to taker means solo; announced at hand end
partner_seat == taker; announced at hand end
led suit L: trump if the led card is 11, 21 or of suit trump, else floor(code/10)
winner of the most recent trick
T: Taker's hand_tricks plus partner's if call (announced at hand end)
d for the hand (announced at hand end)

setup: Every player's score, tricks_won and hand_tricks are 0.
The deck holds the 20 codes 11-15, 21-25, 31-35, 41-45 (code = 10 x suit + rank; suits Spades 1, Clubs 2, Hearts 3, Diamonds 4; ranks A 1, 2 2, J 3, Q 4, K 5).
Cards are always shown to players by name and code (e.g. 11 = Ace of Spades, Spadille; 21 = Ace of Clubs, Baste).

round.effect: round_no += 1; hand_no = ceil(round_no/5); trick_in_hand = round_no - 5*(hand_no-1); priority_seat = ((hand_no-1) mod 4)+1; every played_card = 0 and power = 0

when trick_in_hand == 1: return all cards to deck (deck = all 20 codes, every hand = []), then deal 5 random cards from deck to each player's hand (remove from deck, append to hand); every hand_tricks = 0, bid = 0, is_partner = false
when trick_in_hand == 1: each player is sent their own hand by name and code
when trick_in_hand == 1: bid = 0 for Pass, else the number; all bids announced together

when trick_in_hand == 1: key(seat) = bid*10 + (4 - ((seat - priority_seat) mod 4)); if every bid == 0 then taker = priority_seat and contract = 3, else taker = seat with max key and contract = that seat's bid; announce taker and contract

round.answer: one of 16 options: trump suit (Spades, Clubs, Hearts, Diamonds) x partner seat (1, 2, 3, 4; own seat = solo)
round.effect: when trick_in_hand == 1: trump = chosen suit number; partner_seat = chosen seat; is_solo = (partner_seat == taker); announce trump only
when trick_in_hand == 1 and is_solo == false: is_partner of partner_seat = true; that player alone is privately told 'you are the Taker's partner'
leader = taker if trick_in_hand == 1, else last_winner

round.answer: any card code in the leader's hand
round.effect: leader's played_card = chosen code; remove it from hand; announce the card by name and code
suit(c) = trump if c in {11,21}, else floor(c/10); led_suit = suit(leader's played_card)

round.answer: a card code from own hand: if the hand holds any card with suit(c) == led_suit, only those cards are offered, else any card
round.effect: each responder's played_card = chosen code; remove it from hand
for each player with c = played_card, r = c mod 10: power = 30 if c == 11; 29 if c == 10*trump+2; 28 if c == 21; 20 + r if floor(c/10) == trump; r if suit(c) == led_suit; else 0
last_winner = seat with the highest power (ties impossible); last_winner's tricks_won += 1 and hand_tricks += 1; announce all four cards and the winner

when trick_in_hand == 5: hand_total = taker.hand_tricks + (is_solo ? 0 : partner_seat.hand_tricks); hand_delta = contract-1 if hand_total >= contract; -(contract-1) if hand_total == contract-1; -contract if hand_total <= contract-2
when trick_in_hand == 5: if is_solo then taker.score += 3*hand_delta and each other seat score -= hand_delta; else taker and partner_seat score += hand_delta and the other two score -= hand_delta
when trick_in_hand == 5: announce partner_seat (or that it was a solo), hand_total, hand_delta and all scores
end the game if round_no == 40, else continue

ending.decided_by: Highest score wins; among players tied on score, the one with the most tricks won over the game wins; players still level share the win (a draw).

rules.text: The pack has 20 cards with codes 10 x suit + rank, suits Spades 1, Clubs 2, Hearts 3, Diamonds 4 and ranks A 1, 2 2, J 3, Q 4, K 5; 11 is Spadille and 21 is Baste.
The game has 40 rounds; each round is one trick; hand h covers rounds 5h-4 to 5h, so there are 8 hands of 5 tricks.
The priority seat of hand h is ((h-1) mod 4)+1, giving 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4.
On the first trick of each hand, all 20 cards are shuffled, each player is dealt 5 private cards, and every hand_tricks is set to 0.
On the first trick of each hand, all players bid at once, each choosing Pass, 3, 4 or 5, and all bids are announced.
The highest bid becomes Taker with contract B equal to that bid; ties go to the tied seat first clockwise from the priority seat (key = bid*10 + 4 - ((seat - priority) mod 4)).
When all four players pass, the priority seat is Taker with contract 3.
The Taker privately chooses a trump suit and a partner seat from 16 options, and the trump suit is announced to all.
When the Taker names another seat, the hand is a call and only that seat is privately told it is the partner.
When the Taker names their own seat, the hand is a solo and nobody is told anything beyond the trump suit.
The partner seat stays hidden until the hand ends.
The trumps are every card of the trump suit plus 11 and 21; 11 and 21 count only as the trump suit, and Manille is code 10*trump+2.
The Taker leads the first trick of a hand, and the previous trick's winner leads every later trick.
The led card leaves the leader's hand and is shown to all; the led suit is trump if the card is 11, 21 or of the trump suit, else the card's suit.
The other three players play at once, and a player holding any card of the led suit (11 and 21 count as trump) must play one.
A player holding no card of the led suit may play any card, and illegal cards are never accepted.
Card power is 30 for 11, 29 for Manille, 28 for 21, 20 + rank for other trump-suit cards, the rank for non-trump cards of the led suit, and 0 for any other card.
The highest power wins the trick; all four cards and the winner are announced, and the winner gains 1 tricks_won and 1 hand_tricks.
After the fifth trick of a hand, T is the Taker's hand_tricks plus the partner's hand_tricks if the hand is a call.
When T >= B, d = B-1 (made); when T = B-1, d = -(B-1) (remise); when T <= B-2, d = -B (codille).
In a call, the Taker and the partner each gain d and the other two each lose d.
In a solo, the Taker gains 3d and each of the other three loses d.
After each hand, the partner seat (or solo), T, d and all scores are announced.
There is no talk phase; players communicate only through bids and cards.
After round 40 the game ends: highest score wins, ties on score are broken by most tricks_won, and a further tie is a shared win (draw).

offers.question: Declaration (first trick of each hand)
offers.options: 16 combinations of trump suit (Spades, Clubs, Hearts, Diamonds) and partner seat (1, 2, 3, 4, own seat meaning solo)

offers.question: Lead
offers.options: every card in the leader's hand

offers.question: Follow
offers.who: the three seats other than the leader
offers.options: a seat holding any card of the led suit (11 and 21 counted as trump suit): only those cards; a seat holding none: every card in its hand

choices.why: The designer set 4. The deck (20 cards = 4 x 5), the partner call and the priority rotation are all built for exactly four seats.

The rules forbid discussion; bids and cards are the only signals. A player's strategy lies in bidding to hand strength, choosing a partner who likely holds key trumps, and inferring the hidden partner from play.
tricks_won is at most 40 (under 100), so score dominates and tricks_won only breaks ties; players still level share the win, which serves as the draw.

choices.what: Card power stored as public player attributes
choices.why: Power is computed only from public played cards, so showing it reveals nothing new.

simplifications.what: The deck is rebuilt from all 20 codes at the start of each hand instead of physically gathering the cards
simplifications.why: This is equivalent to gathering and shuffling, since all 20 cards are always played out over the 5 tricks.

simplifications.what: Hand-start and hand-end steps run in every round, gated by conditions on trick_in_hand
simplifications.why: The engine's step list is flat; per-step conditions reproduce the source's 'first trick' and 'fifth trick' steps.
